claim: In the same model at volume fraction 0.010, dipolar coupling above 9 with the active force below a lambda-dependent threshold gives an active gel: a percolated network of branched chains that stays connected while its bonds break and reform faster than in the passive gel, so particles diffuse faster in both translation and rotation. At lambda = 16 the network survives up to f_a = 50 and becomes a string fluid above that.

numbers.name: dipolar_coupling_strength
numbers.note: the coupling above which the gel forms at low active force.

numbers.name: dipolar_coupling_strength
numbers.note: the coupling of the example below.

numbers.name: reduced_active_force
numbers.note: the largest active force at which the lambda = 16 network survives.

validity_conditions: A MODEL RESULT. Three-dimensional overdamped active Brownian spheres with a WCA core and a point magnetic dipole along the propulsion direction, no hydrodynamics; lambda = mu^2/(kT sigma^3), f_a = Fa sigma/kT, gamma_t* = 3 so that the Peclet number va = f_a/3; HOOMD-blue on GPU (version not stated), time step 2e-4 tau with tau = 1/Dr, 8,788 particles, dipole sum without Ewald (see dipolar_active_brownian_spheres_dipole_sum_without_ewald_at_low_density); steady state reached from equilibrated passive systems by raising the active force gradually; states by cluster analysis with a 1.2 sigma neighbour cutoff: gas below half the particles polymerised, string fluid above half with the largest cluster under 70%, percolated network at 70% or more. Three-dimensional volume fraction pi rho*/6: 0.010 at rho* = 0.02 and 0.08 at rho* = 0.15. Reduced density rho* = 0.02; lambda studied up to 16. For lambda at or above 12.25 with f_a = 0 and 10 the dynamics is too slow for the runs to reach equilibrium, so those points are not steady states.
